definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_find_tools
definition.description: Browse Alexandria data providers and workflows or read a selected contract. Alexandria covers companies, people, jobs, finance and filings, public records and government spending, real estate, places and restaurants, retail and prices, package registries and developer data, news, research, and more: typed, sourced records through published contracts. Prefer normal firecrawl_search for a data task; it already returns matching providers. Use this tool when the contract you need was not returned in full, to browse a category when search found nothing, or before scraping the same fields from several pages. Discovery is free. Use query for semantic discovery or urls to find providers for a website. With no arguments, browse categories, then providers and tools. Contracts describe the inputs and outputs for execution through firecrawl_scrape. nextTool identifies further discovery or pagination. Discovery does not execute providers. Use firecrawl_search when you also need web results.

query.description: Semantic lookup of tools for the data you need. Selectors constrain the search.

providers.description: Values from each listed tool's `provider` field (e.g. "apps-apple-com"). Alone, lists that provider's compact tools; with capabilities, scopes them.

categories.description: Category IDs returned by an empty call. Lists providers by default.

groups.description: Optional group IDs for explicit group browsing.

capabilities.description: Values from each listed tool's `capability` field (e.g. "apps/app"). Put the provider in `providers`: {"providers": ["apps-apple-com"], "capabilities": ["apps/app"]}. A selected capability expands its complete contract by default.

level.description: Usually omit: it follows the arguments (tools for query, urls, providers, capabilities or groups; providers for categories; categories with none). Set providers or groups to list those within a category or url scope instead of tools. query, or a non-empty expand with any other argument, returns tools.

expand.description: Use ["options", "response"] for inputs and output shape without example payloads; [] keeps results compact. Omit for full contracts on selected capabilities.

includeCosts.description: Include per-capability credit prices (creditsCost, perRecord) in tool results.

objective.description: The user's underlying goal for this call, in one sentence: what they are ultimately trying to accomplish, not a restatement of the URL or query. Reuse it across related calls. Avoid sensitive information.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_scrape
definition.description:
Scrape one URL and return its content: markdown by default, or HTML, links, screenshots, branding data, or a targeted answer. Use it when the request identifies a page and needs its content or defined fields: the user gives a URL or names a page or PDF and wants it read or summarized, or wants prices, specs, contact details or a table from it. Use `firecrawl_search` when additional web sources are needed. `url` may omit the scheme (`example.com/page`); it is read as https.

Firecrawl may serve recently indexed content; set `maxAge: 0` for a live fetch or a smaller `maxAge` to bound staleness. A successful response does not by itself confirm the page is still current. A named browser profile loads saved session data without saving changes to it.

On an authenticated session, `firecrawl_search` and `firecrawl_find_tools` can discover providers for the same fields across several pages; a matching provider returns typed records in one call.

With `alexandria` in place of `url`, the tool runs catalogued provider capabilities instead of fetching a page. Some providers require accepted terms; when a response reports a terms requirement, direct the user to the Firecrawl dashboard URL in that response.

profile.description: Loads a saved browser profile without saving changes to it.

requestId.description: Idempotency key bound to one Alexandria execution payload. Generated when omitted and returned with the result.

alexandria.description: Catalogued Alexandria capability invocation, mutually exclusive with url. One {provider, capability, options} object or an array of 1-10, with contracts available through firecrawl_search or firecrawl_find_tools. Each call may include version to pin a published workflow; omitting it uses latest. Only requestId and timeout are supported alongside alexandria. The selected contract marks required inputs and any requiresOneOf groups (at least one member per group); it may include example.request/example.response and a key field under response (which may differ from records). Where pagination is declared, its fields govern paging with the same filters; catalogue next is separate from provider pagination. Returns per-capability results in data.alexandria with data, records, or an error with a code; individual capabilities can fail even when the outer response succeeds. Some providers require accepted terms; when a response reports a terms requirement, direct the user to the Firecrawl dashboard URL in that response.

capability.description: Capability address as returned by search or discover, e.g. "series/observations".

version.description: Optional published workflow version. Omit to use the latest version.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

capability.description: Capability address as returned by search or discover, e.g. "series/observations".

version.description: Optional published workflow version. Omit to use the latest version.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

toolDetail.description: URL mode only: domain discovery detail, summary by default; compact returns provider/capability/description, full includes contracts. Ignored with alexandria.

domainTools.description: URL mode only: include domain-matched Alexandria tools for the page in tools on the returned document. Ignored with alexandria.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_search
definition.description:
Use this when you need current or specific information from the web: recent events, latest releases and versions, prices, people and companies, statistics, or any fact that may have changed since your training data or that you are not sure of. Returns ranked results with query-relevant highlights; each web result is a title, URL, and description. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. `includeDomains` and `excludeDomains` are mutually exclusive hostname filters; categories limit result types to `research`, `pdf`, `developer`, or `gov`.

For a programming question, add `categories: ["developer"]`. It searches an index of public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation, and returns the results in `data.web` with `category: "developer"`.

For a legal or regulatory question, `categories: ["gov"]` returns results in `data.web` with `category: "gov"` and cannot be combined with other categories; authenticated sessions also have `firecrawl_gov_search` as the dedicated tool. Verify gov results' issuer, jurisdiction, status, and version before citing current law.

Authenticated search combines web results, semantic tool summaries and domain matches. Use sources: ["alexandria"] for semantic tools only. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only. On an authenticated session, tool matches describe available structured-data capabilities, not executed data. toolDetail: "compact" (default) returns only provider, capability and description; "summary" adds metadata; "full" includes their input and output contracts. firecrawl_scrape with an alexandria body executes a selected capability; firecrawl_find_tools provides catalogue browsing and full contracts.

Returns result groups in `data` and an operation `id` for optional search feedback.

toolDetail.description: Compact by default. Compact returns only provider, capability and description; full includes contracts. Inspect selected compact tools with firecrawl_find_tools providers and capabilities.

query.description: Query for web and semantic tool discovery. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. Catalogue browsing is available through firecrawl_find_tools.

domainTools.description: Include domain-matched tools for result URLs. Defaults to true when Alexandria is combined with web, news or images; semantic-only search leaves domain matching off.

highlights.description: Return query-relevant page excerpts for web and news results when available (default). Highlights appear in web `description` and news `snippet`; otherwise, original snippets are returned. Set to false to keep the original search snippets.

includeDomains.description: Hostnames to restrict results to. Mutually exclusive with excludeDomains.

excludeDomains.description: Hostnames to leave out of results. Mutually exclusive with includeDomains.

sources.description: Search sources; authenticated sessions default to web + alexandria, keyless sessions to web only. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only. enterprise zdr or anon searches do not add it. Use ["alexandria"] alone for provider discovery without web results.

categories.description: Limit results to specific source types. `research` restricts ordinary web results to research-affiliated websites and returns page snippets, which is separate from the `firecrawl_research_*` tools that search paper abstracts and full text across biomedical (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv) and arXiv literature; `pdf` searches PDF results; `developer` searches an index built for coding agents over public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation; `gov` searches the Government Index of US federal, state, and local legal and regulatory sources, the index behind firecrawl_gov_search, and cannot be combined with other categories; gov hits can include historical versions, bill text, agency guidance, and third-party reproductions, so verify the issuer, jurisdiction, enacted/effective status, and version before citing current governing law, clarify a missing jurisdiction or ambiguous as-of date, and use general search for non-US questions or missing coverage (no hits does not establish that no applicable law exists). `developer` and `gov` return hits in `data.web` with `category` set to their name; the other categories also filter `data.web`.

objective.description: The user's underlying goal for this call, in one sentence: what they are ultimately trying to accomplish, not a restatement of the URL or query. Reuse it across related calls. Avoid sensitive information.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_search_feedback
definition.description:
Records schema-validated quality feedback for a prior `firecrawl_search` UUID `searchId`. A `good` rating requires a valuable result or a valuable source, `partial` either of those or at least one `missingContent` entry, and `bad` at least one `missingContent` entry or a query suggestion; caps are 50 `valuableResults`, 50 `valuableSources`, and 20 `missingContent` entries.

Eligibility is limited to successful searches within the feedback age window. The record is idempotent per search ID. Eligible first feedback for a search can refund 1 credit; refunds are subject to the team's daily cap. The response reports whether a refund was applied, along with submission and daily-cap status.

Mark useful returned results in `valuableResults` as `{"source", "position"}` copied off the result. Groups are numbered from 1 independently, so `{"source":"web","position":1}` and `{"source":"news","position":1}` are different results. Be exhaustive — results you do not list are treated as not useful. Reserve `valuableSources` for useful URLs that were NOT among the returned results; never report one result in both fields.

valuableResults.description: Every result that was actually useful, copied from the `source` and `position` stamped on each result. Each group is numbered from 1 independently, so the source is required — `{"source":"web","position":1}` and `{"source":"news","position":1}` are different results. Be exhaustive — unlisted results are treated as not useful. Do not also list the same results in valuableSources.

missingContent.description: Array of specific pieces of content the agent expected to find but did not. One entry per distinct topic. Each entry has a short `topic` and optional longer `description`.

32:CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN=... CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID=... pnpm check:observability --stage dev-yourname
80:## Workers Logs are sampled at 1%
82:The account's Workers Logs are rate limited: `GET /accounts/{id}/observability/usage/limit` (`cf observability usage-limit get`) reports `status: "limited"` and `sample_rate: 0.01`, so Cloudflare keeps a 1% head-based sample of every Worker's events (the documented behaviour once an account passes its daily limit; `resets_at` is null, so do not count on it ending). A single request has a 99% chance of leaving no event. This is why the spike's Main Worker, with logs on and about 25 requests, never showed up.
84:The canary sweep therefore sends its canary 1000 times to each Worker (all lost with probability 0.99^1000 ≈ 4·10⁻⁵). It polls for up to 10 minutes until the Main Worker's canary is found (the positive control), then asserts that the Submission Worker produced zero events and that its canary is in no event. If logging were on, about 10 of its 1000 requests would be kept, so zero is meaningful. Checked on 2026-11-07 on a workers.dev stage: the sweep passed in 90 seconds (12 Main events found), and with the Submission Worker's logs switched on it failed (7 events, canary found).
96:## Deployed observability settings
98:Alchemy turns observability on when the prop is omitted, so the Submission Worker sets every channel off. `check-observability.ts` reads the settings back from the Cloudflare API and fails if `observability.enabled`, `logs.enabled`, `traces.enabled` or `logpush` is on, or a tail consumer is attached. `logs.invocation_logs` and `persist` always read `true` while their channel is off, and no API call changes that (tested with the script-settings and Workers PATCH endpoints), so they count only when their channel is on.

content.thinking:
I think the queue binding and the SendEmail binding are both named "Email", so one has overwritten the other. That means `env.Email` is the Queue producer at runtime, and `client.send(message)` will succeed by enqueuing the email body rather than actually sending it.

If the Queue send returns undefined, then `result.messageId` would throw a TypeError inside the Effect.map, which is a defect rather than a normal failure. That defect would kill the stream and fail the whole consumer batch, so the messages get retried. On retry the claim finds the send still in Sending with an active lease and waits, and once the lease expires the send ends up Failed with an unknown code. The junk email body also lands on the Email queue, where the consumer rejects it as malformed and acks it, and the HTML containing the token passes through the queue as well, which is a privacy concern.

I'm weighing a fix that renames the SendEmail binding so it no longer collides with the Email queue binding, and I'm considering a unit test that checks the two binding names differ. I also want to add a guard so a missing messageId from the send call is treated as an unknown outcome rather than throwing.

I'm checking how the queue's binding name gets derived in the alchemy code, to confirm whether it really comes out as "Email".

The deployed send_email binding and the Email Queue producer both use the name "Email", so only the queue binding survives in production. I'm checking how Alchemy names queue bindings and what Email.test.ts covers next.

I think the queue binding and the SendEmail binding are both named "Email", so one has overwritten the other. That means `env.Email` is the Queue producer at runtime, and `client.send(message)` will succeed by enqueuing the email body rather than actually sending it.

If the Queue send returns undefined, then `result.messageId` would throw a TypeError inside the Effect.map, which is a defect rather than a normal failure. That defect would kill the stream and fail the whole consumer batch, so the messages get retried. On retry the claim finds the send still in Sending with an active lease and waits, and once the lease expires the send ends up Failed with an unknown code. The junk email body also lands on the Email queue, where the consumer rejects it as malformed and acks it, and the HTML containing the token passes through the queue as well, which is a privacy concern.

I'm weighing a fix that renames the SendEmail binding so it no longer collides with the Email queue binding, and I'm considering a unit test that checks the two binding names differ. I also want to add a guard so a missing messageId from the send call is treated as an unknown outcome rather than throwing.

I'm checking how the queue's binding name gets derived in the alchemy code, to confirm whether it really comes out as "Email".

The deployed send_email binding and the Email Queue producer both use the name "Email", so only the queue binding survives in production. I'm checking how Alchemy names queue bindings and what Email.test.ts covers next.

lines: No stage other than `production` can send real mail. To try real sending elsewhere, change `sendsRealEmail` in `packages/cloudflare/src/Email.ts` on a throwaway branch and deploy a personal stage. That stage then also claims `notify.surveybeat.app` and its event subscription, so destroy it before production is deployed.

+**The `send_email` binding is named `SendEmail`.** Binding names share one namespace per Worker. Until #147 it was named `Email`, like the Email queue's producer binding; the deploy kept only the queue, so production queued each rendered email instead of sending it and every send failed as `unknown`. Read the deployed bindings back with `cf workers versions get <version> --worker-id <main worker>` when email stops arriving.

**Send states.** `pending → sending → sent | failed(reason)`. A delivery takes a two-minute lease before calling the provider, and the call times out after 30 seconds. A clear rejection (`E_RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` and other coded errors) returns the send to `pending` and the message is retried after 30 s, 60 s, and 120 s; the fourth rejection fails it. Permanent rejections (`E_RECIPIENT_SUPPRESSED`, sender and header errors) fail at once. An error without a code, a timeout, or a lease that expired with no outcome fails the send as `unknown`, and it is never resent automatically. A message the queue dead-letters fails its send too (`abandoned`, or `rejected` after earlier rejections).

**Bounces and complaints.** Alchemy's `Cloudflare.Queues.Subscription` with the `email.sending` source subscribes the `EmailEvents` queue to `message.bounced`, `message.complained`, `message.rejected`, and `message.failed` for the sending subdomain. The consumer finds the send through the D1 table `email_message` (provider message id → Organization and send) and fails it with the event's reason.

git checkout -q -b fix-147-send-email-binding && git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Fix production email: give the send_email binding its own name

The send_email binding was named "Email", the same name as the Email
queue's producer binding. The deployed production Main Worker kept only
the queue binding, so the consumer's env.Email.send(message) queued the
rendered email instead of sending it, resolved to undefined, and the
send then failed as `unknown` with no message accepted by Cloudflare.

Rename the binding to "SendEmail" and treat a send that returns no
message id as an unknown outcome instead of a crash. Part of #147.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git push -q -u origin fix-147-send-email-binding 2>&1 | tail -2; gh pr create --base main --title "Fix production email: give the send_email binding its own name" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Part of #147 (urgent: the product owner's test email never arrived on production).

## Root cause
`SendEmail = Cloudflare.Email.SendEmail("Email")` used the binding name `Email`, which the Email queue's producer binding (`Queue("Email")`) also uses. The deployed production Main Worker (version e3cf769f, read back with `cf workers versions get`) has a `queue` binding `Email` and **no `send_email` binding at all**. So the queue consumer's `env.Email.send({ from, to, subject, html, text })` hit the Queue producer: it queued the rendered email onto the Email queue (the consumer later dropped it as malformed), resolved to `undefined`, and `result.messageId` threw. The send's lease then expired and it settled as `failed: unknown`. Cloudflare never received a message, which matches the empty `email_message` and `test_invitation_index` tables, an empty `captured_email`, and an empty Email/DLQ backlog. Staging never binds `send_email`, so no test or stage could catch it.

## Change
- Rename the binding to `SendEmail`.
- `cloudflareEmailSender` decodes the send result; a result without a message id is now `EmailOutcomeUnknown("E_NO_MESSAGE_ID")`, not a defect.
- Tests that fail before the fix: the binding name collides with none of the Main Worker's other bindings, and a send that returns no message id is an unknown outcome.
- docs/infra.md notes the naming rule and how to read the deployed bindings back.

After this deploys, "Send me a test" must be pressed again: the earlier send failed as `unknown` and is never resent automatically. The visibility part of #147 (test-send status, failed-emails list) follows in a separate PR.

Checks: `pnpm typecheck`, `typecheck:effect`, `lint`, `format:check`, `pnpm test` (954 passed), `Email.test.ts` on workerd.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -1

For a change to several files at once, or a rewrite of most of a page, use Edit on the file(s), not a shell command, and publish the artifact again with the same `file_path` in the same response: the Edit call(s) first, then the Artifact publish, with no Read and without waiting for the Edit result. The calls run in the order sent, so the publish carries the edited file; a publish sent in the same response as a failed Edit of that file is refused and leaves the artifact as it was, so correct the Edit and publish again. Either way, read the file first only if its text is not in this conversation or you can't place the change exactly from it.

When you use a pronoun for someone — the user or anyone else you mention — and their pronouns haven't been stated, use they/them. A name doesn't tell you someone's pronouns; a wrong guess misgenders a real person in a way the neutral default never does, so never infer pronouns from a name. This applies to all user-visible text, including visible thinking.

For actions that are hard to reverse or outward-facing, confirm first unless durably authorized or explicitly told to proceed without asking; approval in one context doesn't extend to the next. Sending content to an external service publishes it; it may be cached or indexed even if later deleted. Before deleting or overwriting, look at the target. Report outcomes faithfully: if tests fail, say so with the output; if a step was skipped, say that; when something is done and verified, state it plainly without hedging.

# Memory

You have a persistent file-based memory at `/home/ubuntu/.claude/projects/-home-ubuntu-surveybeat-next/memory/`. This directory already exists — write to it directly with the Write tool (do not run mkdir or check for its existence). Each memory is one file holding one fact, with frontmatter:

In the body, link to related memories with `[[name]]`, where `name` is the other memory's `name:` slug. Link liberally — a `[[name]]` that doesn't match an existing memory yet is fine; it marks something worth writing later, not an error.

`user`: who the user is (role, expertise, preferences). `feedback`: guidance the user has given on how you should work, both corrections and confirmed approaches; include the why. `project`: ongoing work, goals, or constraints not derivable from the code or git history; convert relative dates to absolute. `reference`: pointers to external resources (URLs, dashboards, tickets).

After writing the file, add a one-line pointer in `MEMORY.md` (`- [Title](file.md) — hook`). `MEMORY.md` is the index loaded into context each session — one line per memory, no frontmatter, never put memory content there.

Before saving, check for an existing file that already covers it. Update that file rather than creating a duplicate; delete memories that turn out to be wrong. Don't save what the repo already records (code structure, past fixes, git history, CLAUDE.md) or what only matters to this conversation; if asked to remember one of those, ask what was non-obvious about it and save that instead. # Environment

# Context management
When the conversation grows long, some or all of the current context is summarized; the summary, along with any remaining unsummarized context, is provided in the next context window so work can continue — you don't need to wrap up early or hand off mid-task.

When you have enough information to act, act. Do not re-derive facts already established in the conversation, re-litigate a decision the user has already made, or narrate options you will not pursue. If you are weighing a choice, give a recommendation, not an exhaustive survey

When you plan several searches, send them in the same turn.

You can embed images, video, and audio in your response using Markdown image syntax with absolute file paths. Link each PR you create, take over, or push to: link_pull_request, or link_pull_requests for several, full URL, every stack layer, as your next call. Host tools do not link for you. If linking fails, say so. Skip PRs you only read or review, and PRs named only as background.
